newsitem.title: USA: Entergy sees EPS at low end of estimates.
newsitem.headline: Entergy sees EPS at low end of estimates.

text.p: Entergy Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Ed Lupberger on Friday said he expects earnings per share for the upcoming quarter and the year to come in at the lower end of analysts' estimates.
"I think the high side of the range is a little too optimistic," he said. "I think the lower end of the range is probably more realistic."
Analysts expect the company to generate between $0.80 and $0.86 a share in the second quarter and $2.50 to $2.70 a share earnings for the year, according to First Call.
"I am comfortable we can generate five percent growth in earnings per share through 1998," he said.
Lupberger said analysts may have boosted their earnings estimates based on projections of expected results from its February 1997 acquisition of London Electricity.
"I believe some analysts included their assessment of the impact of London on us. But we haven't been there long enough to assess that for ourselves this year," he said.
Lupberger said the company is exploring options for diversifying its business base ahead of deregulation of the domestic electric industry.

"There is no doubt we can't maintain our old customer levels under competition. We have to look to areas where growth is possible," he said, referring to privatization of international power grids and opportunies to sell other niche services like communications to existing domestic customers.
The New Orleans-based electric and natural gas company posted $1.83 a share consolidated net income in 1996, including unusual items that decreased earnings by $147.92 million or $0.65 a share.
